bills.title: REPAIR Act
bills.full_title: Right to Equitable and Professional Auto Industry Repair Act
bills.summary: Requires auto and powersports manufacturers to share telematics data, repair data, and diagnostic tools with independent repair shops and vehicle owners on fair and reasonable terms.
bills.briefing: This bill directly affects your right to have your bike serviced by an independent shop or fix it yourself. If passed, manufacturers — including motorcycle OEMs — can no longer lock repair data, telematics access, and diagnostic tools behind dealer-only networks. A win for every rider who's ever been told 'only a dealer can do that.'

bills.title: Stop Motorcycle Profiling Act
bills.summary: Directs the Department of Justice to issue guidance to state and local law enforcement agencies addressing discriminatory traffic stops and searches of motorcyclists based solely on their motorcycle affiliation.
bills.briefing: This bill targets a real and documented problem: riders getting pulled over, searched, and harassed simply for wearing a patch or riding a specific style of bike. The DOJ guidance would establish a federal standard that law enforcement must follow — no more pretextual stops based on your ride.

bills.title: Stop Motorcycle Profiling Act (House)
bills.summary: House companion to S.1424. Directs DOJ to issue guidance ending discriminatory stops targeting motorcyclists.
bills.briefing: Companion to the Senate bill. Having both chambers with active bills increases the odds of movement — but this one needs more cosponsors to gain traction. The AMA is actively lobbying for both.

bills.title: Texas Lane Filtering (HB 1927)
bills.full_title: Texas House Bill 1927 — Motorcycle Lane Filtering
bills.summary: Permits motorcyclists to filter between lanes of slow or stopped traffic at speeds below 20 mph when traffic is moving below 10 mph. Modeled after Utah's successful 2019 law.
bills.briefing: Texas passing lane filtering would be the biggest state win for riders since Utah legalized it in 2019. It reduces rear-end collision risk for riders and eases traffic. Passed committee 8–3 — heading to a full House vote. If Texas passes, expect a domino effect in other large states.

bills.title: Ohio Helmet Choice (HB 244)
bills.full_title: Ohio House Bill 244 — Adult Motorcycle Helmet Choice
bills.summary: Would repeal Ohio's universal helmet requirement for riders 21 and older who carry adequate insurance coverage. Retains helmet requirement for riders under 21.
bills.briefing: Ohio has had universal helmet coverage since 1978. This bill would restore adult choice — a longstanding AMA and ABATE position. Michigan made a similar move in 2012. Ohio insurance carriers are lobbying against it.

bills.title: Minnesota Lane Filtering (HF 1623)
bills.full_title: Minnesota House File 1623 — Motorcycle Lane Filtering
bills.summary: Allows motorcyclists to lane filter between stopped or slow-moving vehicles on roads with speed limits of 55 mph or less.
bills.briefing: Minnesota has been trying to pass lane filtering for three sessions. This iteration has more cosponsors than previous attempts and a stronger safety argument backed by new crash data from Utah and Montana.
